title.narrative: Addressing Gendered Disinformation by Engaging Men and Boys

description.narrative:
In an increasingly digital world, gendered disinformation and other harmful online behaviours pose a growing threat to gender equality and democratisation worldwide. Within the 'Manosphere', a collection of online spaces where misogynistic narratives, attitudes, and harmful gender norms are shared and amplified, coordinated disinformation campaigns that discredit women, women's rights, and gender equality spread rapidly and at scale. Men and boys are disproportionately represented among those who enable this content, yet are themselves subject to the harmful consequences of rigid masculine gender norms.
This activity aims to strengthen men and boys in recognising, rejecting, and responding to gendered disinformation and other harmful online behaviour that undermines gender equality and the safety of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. To do so, it will establish a grant system to identify and support initiatives across non-EU Eastern Europe and sub-Saharan Africa. Grants will support the development and scaling of digital prevention tools and pilot interventions designed to challenge harmful gender norms and promote positive digital masculinities. Interventions may include training sessions on identifying harmful gender norms, game-based approaches, online campaigns, and innovative digital tools such as a computer-based masculinities and a harm microsimulation lab. By engaging men and boys as active partners in prevention, the programme seeks not only to reduce harm to others, but to benefit men and boys themselves. In doing so, it aims to ease social pressures that encourage harmful behaviour, foster more positive peer relationships, and contribute to safer, more respectful digital environments for everyone.
To achieve this, the activity will begin with a landscaping analysis and regional research, the findings of which will inform both implementing countries and partners. This foundation will guide the grant-making system, focusing on three pillars: *Critical Digital Literacy: funding context-specific training and educational materials to equip men and boys to identify harmful gender narratives and behaviours, report them, and engage more critically with gendered disinformation online; *Policy and Corporate Advocacy: strengthening civil society organisations to advocate for platform accountability and legislative frameworks that protect the digital rights of women, girls, and marginalised groups, driving systemic change at the structural level; *Caring Online Spaces: co-designing interventions with men and boys that actively reward positive peer norms and inclusive digital masculinities, creating digital environments where healthy behaviour is the norm rather than the exception.
This activity is a pilot initiative that will be implemented over a period of 25 months. By supporting this activity, the MFA will build knowledge on how gendered disinformation manifests in non-EU Eastern Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, gain insight into which (digital) interventions are most effective in engaging men and boys, and better determine its future engagement and positioning on this theme.
